declared_purpose: Provide an OpenClaw credential-security workflow: discover credentials, back up originals, consolidate into ~/.openclaw/.env, apply mode 600 and Git protection, validate, and clean up migrated files. The entry declares centralization mandatory; supporting policy requires encrypted backups and minimized access. These requirements do not prescribe unrestricted JSON-field migration, bulk credential exports, or value logging (SKILL.md:3-16, 40-48; CORE-PRINCIPLE.md:29-52).

data_operations.operation: Discover and inspect local files; infer whether they contain credentials
data_operations.data_scope: Matching configuration, memory, workspace, skills, scripts and local-share files; additional user patterns; existing root .env. JSON is parsed completely, but classification examines top-level key names. Env files are read line by line to collect variable names. Results include paths, keys, sizes, modes and errors. Read failures are classified as likely credentials.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Scanner memory and its local caller; no file persistence in the scanner.
data_operations.condition: Called directly or by consolidation/cleanup. Dispatch accepts JSON and names ending in .env; ordinary .env.production and shell rc files are skipped despite matching advertised patterns. ~/.env is absent from default patterns.

data_operations.data_scope: Text output exposes paths, types, modes, counts and up to five key names per file. JSON output includes all returned key names, metadata and errors.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output of the invoking process; subsequent capture or retention is unknown.
data_operations.condition: Direct CLI execution; imported scan_locations returns results to its caller without this CLI reporting.

data_operations.operation: Load, classify and normalize migration data locally
data_operations.data_scope: Existing root credentials and complete parsed candidate files. Service is inferred from path substrings, key names and sometimes API-key contents. Every top-level field is eligible for normalization, including mapped account identifiers and unmapped fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Consolidation-process dictionaries; paths, inferred services and key mappings also reach standard output.
data_operations.condition: All candidates are scanned and loaded before the service filter is applied. Backup-only mode also performs loading and normalization. Existing root keys take precedence; later candidates can replace earlier pending values for the same new key.

data_operations.data_scope: Complete credential files, including unrelated contents, comments and filesystem metadata; copies are not redacted or encrypted by this function.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/backups/credentials-old-YYYYMMDD/*.bak; source and destination paths are printed.
data_operations.condition: Existing root .env is copied before change confirmation. Selected source files are copied after confirmation, with --yes, or without confirmation in --backup-only mode. Day-based destinations and reused filenames can overwrite previous copies. Cleanup does not delete these backups.

data_operations.operation: Write consolidated credentials and supporting files
data_operations.data_scope: Existing credentials plus new normalized fields and their values. The template contains variable names with placeholders, not copied values. Git configuration receives an .env exclusion.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/.env, ~/.openclaw/.env.example and ~/.openclaw/.gitignore; completion paths and counts return to the local caller.
data_operations.condition: After confirmation or --yes, when new keys exist and backup-only is false. Mode 600 is applied after writing the credential file. Git protection is decided by a substring check.

data_operations.operation: Validate local content and protection; optionally change permissions and Git exclusions
data_operations.data_scope: Root .env permissions, key/value syntax, duplicates, placeholder-like content and total content size; .gitignore text. Reports contain counts, key names and warnings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Validation-process memory and standard output. --fix changes .env mode and writes .gitignore entries.
data_operations.condition: According to --check; default all performs the content and metadata checks. The validator does not scan for scattered credential files.

data_operations.operation: Enforce protection checks and return one requested credential
data_operations.data_scope: Root .env existence and mode, .gitignore text, and credential-file lines until the requested key is found.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The requested value returns to the importing caller. Failures print security metadata or the requested variable name to standard error.
data_operations.condition: get_credential first requires successful security checks. Direct enforce.py execution checks metadata and reports status without loading credential values.

data_operations.operation: List and delete discovered non-root source files
data_operations.data_scope: Every existing scanner result except ~/.openclaw/.env; deletion removes the entire file, including any noncredential contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Original filesystem paths are unlinked; paths, errors and counts reach standard output. Credential backups remain.
data_operations.condition: Default is a listing-only dry run. Deletion requires --confirm and the exact DELETE response. The --force option is not forwarded to bypass that response. No successful migration or per-file backup check is required.

data_operations.operation: Documented bulk loading into execution environments
data_operations.data_scope: Every parsed credential variable in the root .env, although the examples subsequently use one SERVICE_API_KEY.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python process environment or Bash shell; the export recipes also make credentials available through inherited child-process environments.
data_operations.condition: Only when a consumer adopts these documentation snippets. The consolidation executable does not perform these exports.

data_operations.data_scope: Full SERVICE_API_KEY in Bash examples; an API-key prefix in the recommended logging example; matching staged-diff lines, potentially including complete credentials, in the precommit command.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output of the adopted example or command; no remote recipient or log storage is specified.
data_operations.condition: Only if these documentation recipes are executed. Staged-diff exposure requires matching credential-bearing changes.

data_operations.operation: Documented encryption, decryption and backup persistence
data_operations.data_scope: Root credential-file contents; the entire ~/.openclaw directory for encrypted archives; home-directory contents except the primary .env for the general-backup recipe.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GPG output, plaintext /tmp/.env, encrypted backup.tar.gz.gpg, restored archive paths, or local /backup/, depending on the recipe.
data_operations.condition: Optional commands only. The general-backup exclusion covers the primary .env but does not exclude credential-backup directories or scattered source files.

data_operations.data_scope: Timestamp, shell user name and a claim that .env was accessed; no credential value.
data_operations.condition: Only if the manual command is adopted. It is not an automatic access monitor; retention is unspecified.

data_operations.data_scope: A bearer token in an Authorization header.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The endpoint represented by url; no actual endpoint is supplied.
data_operations.condition: Only if a consumer adopts the example and supplies an endpoint. This is not invoked by the packaged credential-management scripts; downstream processing is unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated top-level JSON fields, beyond credentials and necessary companion identifiers/configuration.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/.env values, plus corresponding variable names in .env.example and console mappings.
potential_excess.condition: A detected, selected JSON file contains unrelated fields. One sensitive-looking key can qualify the file, after which all fields are normalized.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Centralizing credentials is required; unrestricted migration of every JSON field is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Persist credentials and companion fields needed for the migrated services.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Select credential fields and required companion fields explicitly; review unknown fields before persisting them. Generate the template from that selected set.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain required usernames, account identifiers and configuration. Preserve complete originals in protected rollback backups when exact restoration is required.

potential_excess.data_scope: The complete existing root credential set and its metadata.
potential_excess.condition: Ordinary consolidation subsequently cancels or finds no new keys. The root backup has already occurred.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A backup protects a pending modification; these branches perform no credential-file modification. This is a redundant persistence action, rather than extra fields in a necessary backup.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Back up the root file before an approved write, or when explicitly requested through backup-only mode.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Defer the root backup until a nonempty migration plan is confirmed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Create the backup before any write and preserve explicit backup-only behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete plaintext originals and old credential versions retained outside the consolidated file.
potential_excess.condition: Any backup is created. copy2 performs no encryption and preserves source permission metadata; cleanup leaves backups in place without an expiry mechanism.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Rollback backups are explicitly required, but supporting policy requires encrypted backups and minimized access. Plaintext retention is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Maintain recoverable originals through validation and application testing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Persist encrypted rollback copies with restrictive access instead of plaintext copies; provide a retention policy after successful migration.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep complete recoverable originals for the required rollback period. Do not redact backups needed for exact restoration or remove the sole recovery copy prematurely.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unmigrated, unreadable or mixed-content files, including sources previously skipped by a service filter or existing-key conflict.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Original non-root files selected for unlinking by cleanup.py.
potential_excess.condition: Cleanup is confirmed. Selection depends on scanner results and existence, without checking successful migration, value equivalence or a recoverable per-file backup.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared cleanup purpose is removing old files after migration; deleting unverified files exceeds that condition.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Remove credential originals that are demonstrably obsolete after successful migration and testing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Delete only files recorded in a verified migration manifest; check recoverability and preserve unmigrated or unrelated contents.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain failed, filtered and conflicting sources until resolved. Continue allowing explicit cleanup of successfully migrated originals.

potential_excess.data_scope: All stored credentials when a consumer requires only one service credential.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The adopting process environment and inherited environments of child processes.
potential_excess.condition: Consumers use the documented Python bulk loader or Bash export recipe.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Loading from the centralized file is required; exporting its entire contents is not. Supporting policy limits access to necessary processes.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Make requested credentials available to the authorized consuming component.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use selected-key loading such as get_credential and pass an explicit credential allowlist to children.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve security validation and supply all credentials genuinely required by the consumer.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full credential values, credential prefixes, or credential-bearing staged-diff lines.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Standard output from documented loading, logging and precommit recipes.
potential_excess.condition: Those optional examples are adopted; matching staged changes are present for the precommit command.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Credential use and security auditing do not require displaying secret values. The supporting policy explicitly prohibits full-credential logging.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report successful loading or identify suspect files and locations.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove credential echoes and prefix logging; report variable names/status or filenames and line numbers with values redacted.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the actual credential available to its authorized caller and preserve actionable audit locations.

potential_excess.condition: The optional GPG decryption recipe is executed. It specifies no restrictive creation mode or deletion step.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Decrypting for authorized use can be necessary; retaining an additional plaintext temporary file is a recipe choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Make decrypted credentials available for the required use.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Decrypt into the protected canonical destination when restoring, or use memory/a restricted temporary file removed after use.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the encrypted source and provide the authorized consumer with usable credentials; verify permissions before writing plaintext.

potential_excess.data_scope: Credential rollback copies and remaining scattered credential files included in a general home backup.
potential_excess.condition: The documented rsync recipe is adopted while those files exist. Only the primary ~/.openclaw/.env is excluded.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The recipe is presented as excluding sensitive material from general backups; additional plaintext credential copies defeat that purpose. This is extra data within the backup action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Back up ordinary home data while protecting credential recovery separately.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Exclude the credential-backup subtree and known scattered credential sources, or include only their encrypted archives.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue backing up noncredential data and maintain a separate recoverable encrypted credential backup.

unknowns: No packaged-source inspection blocker remains. Actual deployment contents, execution results, file ownership, ACLs, umask, symlinks and backup recoverability cannot be established from source alone.

Complete discovery and migration cannot be certified: advertised patterns exceed actual dispatch coverage, and validation does not verify that scattered credentials are gone (scripts/scan.py:14-26, 124-139; scripts/validate.py:128-201).
Behavior of the unprovided load_credentials helper and downstream consuming skills is unresolved (SKILL.md:314-319). Normal credential returns do not establish further disclosure.
The optional network example supplies no endpoint or recipient policy. No remote disclosure, telemetry or service interaction is established for the packaged credential-management executables.
Caller capture of console output, external encryption of generated backups, backup retention requirements and downstream access-log retention are unspecified.
